name: Prompt Composer
summary: A chat-style input where Enter sends, Shift+Enter newlines, drafts survive failure, and submission gating never locks the user out of typing.
problem: A chat composer looks like a text field but carries app-level semantics: Enter submits, overturning a decades-old newline convention that must then be re-taught; drafts hold real work that naive implementations destroy on failure; token budgets impose limits that native maxLength enforces by silently eating keystrokes; and IME users get messages fired mid-composition because Enter confirms a character, not a message.
useWhen: Users compose conversational or prompt input submitted to a model
Multi-line input is meaningful and Enter-to-send is the expected convention
Input length is budgeted and users need to see and fix overage themselves
dontUseWhen: The input is a conventional form field where Enter-to-submit would break form semantics
Input is single-line and short, where a standard search-style field is honest
Submission is gated on complex validation better served by an explicit form with inline errors

anatomy.description: The multiline text area where the user composes; grows with content.
Visible button that submits; never the only path (Enter also submits) and never removed when unavailable.
Visible hint teaching the Enter / Shift+Enter mapping.
Remaining-budget display shown when a length limit exists; announces the over-limit transition.

states.description: Nothing to submit; the submit control is present but unavailable.
A draft exists and is within budget; submission is available.
The draft exceeds the length budget; typing continues, submission is gated.
A submission is in flight; typing continues, a second submission is gated.

constraints.statement: The composer input MUST have an accessible name from a visible label or equivalent; placeholder text alone is not an accessible name.
constraints.rationale: Placeholders vanish on input and are inconsistently exposed by assistive technology, leaving the primary control of the product unnamed.
constraints.verification: Unit test: the textarea is reachable by role with its accessible name; axe reports no label violations.

constraints.statement: The composer MUST map Enter to submit and Shift+Enter to inserting a newline.
constraints.rationale: This is the established convention for chat-style AI input; deviating from it breaks muscle memory trained by every major chat product.
constraints.verification: Unit test: Enter triggers the submit callback with the draft; Shift+Enter does not submit.

constraints.statement: The composer MUST NOT treat Enter as submit while an input-method (IME) composition session is active.
constraints.rationale: For CJK and other IME users, Enter confirms a character conversion; submitting mid-composition fires half-written messages and makes the product unusable in those languages.
constraints.verification: Unit test: a keydown Enter event with isComposing true does not invoke the submit callback.

constraints.statement: The composer MUST NOT discard an unsubmitted draft except on explicit user clearing or successful submission.
constraints.rationale: Drafts are work; losing one to a failed submission or busy-state transition converts a transient fault into retyping.
constraints.verification: Unit test: the draft value is unchanged across busy transitions and after a rejected submission attempt.

constraints.statement: The composer MUST NOT silently truncate or block input beyond the length budget; it shows the over-limit state and lets the user edit their way back.
constraints.rationale: Native maxLength swallows keystrokes and pasted content without telling the user what was lost; an explicit over-limit state preserves their text and their agency.
constraints.verification: Unit test: input beyond the budget is fully retained, the over-limit state is exposed, and submission is gated.

constraints.statement: Typing MUST remain possible while submission is unavailable — empty, over limit, or in flight; only submission itself is gated.
constraints.rationale: Users fix overage by editing and compose their next message while the previous one sends; a disabled textarea blocks both for no safety gain.
constraints.verification: Unit test: the textarea is never disabled or readonly in any state.

constraints.statement: When submission is unavailable the submit control MUST remain visible and focusable, exposing the unavailable state and its reason accessibly.
constraints.rationale: A vanished or natively-disabled button is undiscoverable to screen reader users, who are left wondering whether the product can send at all and why it currently will not.
constraints.verification: Unit test: in empty, over-limit, and busy states the button is in the document with aria-disabled true and an accessible description naming the reason.

constraints.statement: The Enter and Shift+Enter mapping SHOULD be visibly hinted near the composer.
constraints.rationale: The mapping contradicts the textarea's native behavior; an invisible convention punishes exactly the users who haven't learned it yet.
constraints.verification: Manual review: a visible hint near the composer states the mapping.

constraints.statement: The composer SHOULD grow vertically with content up to a bounded height rather than confining input to a single scrolling line.
constraints.rationale: Prompts are routinely multi-paragraph; editing inside a one-line slit hides context and produces errors users cannot see.
constraints.verification: Manual review: the input's height tracks content up to a maximum, then scrolls.

constraints.statement: Implementations MAY offer a preference to swap the Enter mapping (for example Ctrl+Enter to send) for accessibility or international input needs.
constraints.rationale: Some users — switch-device users, heavy IME users — are better served by an explicit-modifier send; a preference respects that without changing the default.
constraints.verification: Code review: the preference, if present, persists and is honored by the keydown handling.

wcagCriteria.name: Labels or Instructions
wcagCriteria.relevance: The composer needs a real label, and the non-native Enter mapping is an instruction that must be provided.

wcagCriteria.name: Keyboard
wcagCriteria.relevance: Composing, submitting, and reaching the submit control must all work without a pointer.

wcagCriteria.name: Name, Role, Value
wcagCriteria.relevance: The submit control's unavailable state must be programmatically determinable, not just visually grayed.

keyboard.action: Submits the draft when submission is available; ignored during IME composition.
Moves from the composer to the submit control in document order.

screenReader.behavior: Announces the accessible name and the Enter mapping instructions via the described-by hint.
Polite announcement of the over-limit status from the length-status region.

screenReader.when: Submit control receives focus while unavailable
screenReader.behavior: Announces the control's name, its unavailable state, and the reason (empty, over limit, or sending).

accessibility.focusManagement: Focus stays in the composer after submission so the next message can be typed immediately; the component never moves focus itself.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Height growth is not animated under prefers-reduced-motion; the composer resizes instantly.

do: Keep the submit button visible in every state; communicate unavailability through state, not absence.
Show the length budget only when one exists, and count down visibly as the user approaches it.
Clear the draft only after the host confirms the submission was accepted.
dont: Do not set the native maxLength attribute; it silently eats keystrokes and pasted text.
Do not disable the textarea while a message sends.
Do not rely on placeholder text as the label or as the keyboard hint.

references.title: MDN: KeyboardEvent.isComposing
references.note: The check that keeps Enter-to-send from firing during IME composition.
